findings.title: Stale test function name after type rename
findings.body: The test function is still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware on line 21 even though the type was renamed to MetricsMiddleware. The test name should be updated to TestMetricsMiddleware to match the renamed type and avoid confusion for future maintainers.

findings.title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware has no test coverage
findings.body: The newly added ContextualLoggerMiddleware (NewContextualLoggerMiddleware at line 14, with the underlying ContextualLoggerMiddleware type at line 22) has no associated test file. This middleware is responsible for adding endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, and uname to the request context via log.WithContextualAttributes. The LoggerMiddleware now relies on this behavior to produce logs with those fields. Without tests, there is no verification that these attributes are correctly added, and a future change to instrumentContext could silently break the logger output without any test failure.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext silently discards context
findings.body: TestLogger.FromContext (line 46) ignores the context argument and returns a fresh NewTestLogger() instance, dropping any contextual attributes set via log.WithContextualAttributes. With LoggerMiddleware now using m.logger.FromContext(ctx) instead of m.logger, tests that use TestLogger can no longer verify that contextual attributes (endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname) added by ContextualLoggerMiddleware are actually retrieved by the logger. A test that asserts these fields appear in a log message will fail to do so through this fake, so the new context-propagation logic is effectively untestable.

findings.title: Logger name 'plugin.instrumentation' is misleading after rename
findings.body: The logger is created with the name 'plugin.instrumentation' on line 161 (log.New('plugin.instrumentation')). After renaming InstrumentationMiddleware to MetricsMiddleware and splitting out the contextual logger middleware, this logger name no longer aligns with the new terminology and will be confusing to operators searching logs by component name. Consider updating to 'plugin.logger' or 'plugin.request'.
